summary: The clay jars and sun-disc staff communicate their roles well, and the High Priest has convincing authority. However, most everyday outfits still read as modern shirts and trousers with costume panels attached. The trader is too close to the elder, and several garments lack convincing shoulder attachment.
problems: Orange and green shirt sleeves, blue trouser legs and blocky closed footwear remain conspicuous. Linen aprons over these defaults do not establish an unmistakable Bronze Age.
The four everyday kits share almost the same body silhouette. Their distinction relies heavily on handheld objects and small front details that will weaken at stream scale.
The water carrier's chest wrap reads as a disconnected rectangular patch. The weaver's shoulder wrap reads as a chest stripe, while the elder's shawl resembles two stiff vest panels.
The field tender's sun cloth presents as a tall rectangular slab rather than cloth resting on the crown and draping behind the neck.
The trader repeats the elder's pale cap and paired front panels. Its lapis strip and delicate scales are insufficient to establish a visibly foreign caravan leader.
Solid hip-mounted skirt boxes and the priest's long rigid robe need gait testing: they enclose both leg paths and risk visible leg penetration during movement.
fix: Water Carrier: Remove the exposed modern shirt and trouser treatment; use a short linen wrap, bare lower legs and strapped sandals. Connect the diagonal chest cloth continuously over one shoulder to its back section, fitted close to the torso. Keep the excellent clay jar and make the tied bun visible above the hair silhouette. Field Tender: Use a distinct sleeveless, knee-length belted tunic with bare arms and shins. Flatten the crown cloth and extend a fitted rear neck drape, eliminating the tall slab silhouette. Thicken the hoe shaft and enlarge its bronze blade slightly. Reed Weaver: Replace the modern shirt-and-apron read with a short woven wrap and a broad, connected one-shoulder mantle. Keep its hem distinctly shorter than the tender's. Give the basket a chunky raised rim and broad woven bands rather than tiny surface details. Village Elder: Join the front shawl panels across the shoulders into one continuous wool garment; broaden the upper-back silhouette and add a substantial contrasting hem. Replace visible trousers with an appropriate long wrap and sandals; retain the walking stick. High Priest: Preserve the tall sun staff, tiered headwrap and oversized bronze medallion. Fit the diagonal sash flush around the torso and shoulder instead of reading as a rigid board. Segment and skin the robe for walking, keeping its long ceremonial silhouette without trapping both legs inside a rigid shell. River Trader: Establish a separate foreign silhouette with a broad asymmetric fringed mantle, bold stripes continuing over the shoulders, and a banded headwrap unlike the priest's or elder's. Enlarge the lapis collar into a readable upper-chest shape and thicken the balance beam, supports and pans. Replace modern sleeves, trousers and footwear. Across all kits, use hollow fitted garment shells, attach cloth convincingly at shoulders and waist, and validate both avatar variants in motion at the actual 40-degree stream view.
